elements.title: Carcass Front
elements.description:
A live campaign tracker for Trench Crusade: the map, warbands, rounds of battles and
the weather over them. One SvelteKit app, PostgreSQL for every record, Redis for
what is shared between instances.

elements.title: Request pipeline
elements.description:
Runs on every request, in order: read the session (and roll a remembered cookie),
apply the access gate, count activity, resolve, invalidate the cached snapshot after
a change, write the admin audit entry. `init` runs once at start: migrations, the
.env admin, rules, the Faction Studio seed, zones and the weather timer.

views.title: Access and sign-in
views.description:
**Two modes, two doors.** `ACCESS=open` (a LAN at the venue) lets anyone watch the map;
`ACCESS=private` (deployed; set by build_and_update.sh when DOMAIN is set) shows a
signed-out visitor only the doors: /login, /admin/login and /join/<invite>. Pages
redirect there, data answers 401.

**Decisions**
- One pure function, `accessFor(mode, request, user)`, decides every request; hooks only
  carry it out. Denied pages raise their status in the group layouts, so the book-page
  error page renders inside the app.
- Players sign in at /login, the Campaign Master only at /admin/login. Each door refuses
  the other's accounts with the same answer as a wrong password.
- The CM's door limits per address only, so nobody can lock the CM out by guessing;
  guessing from many addresses meets the long .env password.
- A player on /admin gets a 403 page, never a redirect (no loop); after sign-in a visitor
  returns to `next` only if they may open it.
- Sessions roll forward once a day while in use; a remembered cookie rolls with them.
- A temporary password reaches only Settings until it is replaced.

views.title: Campaign flow
views.description:
**From founding to the final reckoning.** Stages run setup → mustering → underway →
ended (`campaign-flow.ts`, shared by server and pages).

**Decisions**
- Seats come first: the CM sizes the campaign, each seat gets an invite link (single use,
  seven days), and joining makes the account and seats it.
- A campaign needs at least two warbands to get under way; the CM can override other
  mustering checks.
- Rounds of battles: players roll for Aggressor, Aggressors pick opponents and battlefields,
  battles roll Hell on Earth. Each step holds a Postgres advisory lock, so a double tap or
  a player and the CM at once can't act twice.
- The campaign state is replayed from its events (games and adjustments) by the pure rules
  engine, on the server and in the browser alike.

views.title: Live map
views.description:
**Every screen follows the campaign within a second.** A change anywhere (a battle
recorded, the weather turned) reaches every phone and the TV without a reload.

**Decisions**
- The public snapshot is the only campaign view that leaves the server; Vision cards and
  hidden progress never enter it.
- Built once per change and shared: a promise memo in the process, Redis across instances,
  keyed by the campaign's generation.
- Two channels: a change re-sends the whole snapshot; a trigger (a battle result) is a
  one-shot effect every screen plays at the same moment (clock skew is corrected).
- Live updates go through the hub: Redis pub/sub (cf:bus) when REDIS_URL is set, memory otherwise.
- The map draws with PixiJS; effects (sky, bombardment, aircraft) load only in the browser.
- Inside a battle, zooming out below about 55% or panning about 45% of the screen away
  returns to the map; the camera stays where the viewer took it.

views.title: Warband builder and Trench Companion import
views.description:
**Every warband follows the books.** The rules come from book packs: complete Faction Studio files
for each faction and variant (units, armoury, upgrades, faction rules, keywords), read from the
group's own copies of the books and loaded in Admin → Rules. The builder checks each recruit,
purchase and upgrade against them.

**Decisions**
- A variant's entry replaces the faction's entry of the same name; its rules merge onto the
  faction's (upgrades and caps by name, exclusions add up), and excluding a name takes away a unit,
  an armoury item or an upgrade.
- An entry may price an item itself (the Yeoman's rifle); upgrades have a currency and the entries
  they are for. A Leader is required only where a variant names one.
- A Trench Companion warband comes in from a link, its JSON or its text export. Each model is matched
  to its entry (by name, Trench Companion's id, or the rule that names it), each item to the armoury;
  Trench Companion's prices are kept, what doesn't match is kept and reported, and the result is
  checked like any warband.
- Loading packs keeps the Campaign Master's Studio edits.
